title: World Whore Z
summary: Chapter 24 opens with a Mangchi stepfather song, then becomes an extended self-audit of DVDASA as a product: the cast knows it lacks regular scheduling, booking, topics, writers, planning and conventional production, and that its porn association deters guests. Andrew's prior nuanced suicide testimony is immediately compressed into a heroic 'saved his life' claim, illustrating the archive's need to preserve full chronology rather than slogans. The central Morgan Lee sequence is a four-stage record. First, the show changes times, repeatedly lies that Asa will attend, makes talk/nudity part of booking, and threatens future access when work, traffic and family logistics interfere. Second, Morgan sends an old real rental-car crash photo as if current; embedded metadata supports that it is old, and she later directly admits choosing it. Third, before she arrives the room celebrates, insults her, speculates about cocaine and family lies, invents a vendor story, exposes location metadata, and cheers while she cries. Only the crash timing is proven false. Her family problems, mother's health and possible brother incident remain private and unresolved; her denial of drug use controls over peer diagnosis. Fourth, she arrives, acknowledges the lie, explains the old crash and current distress, answers the room, declines face-sitting and butt-smelling, and is explicitly welcomed back. Any summary that omits the scheduling/deception, direct testimony or reversal is editorially invalid. The episode also contains strong privacy lessons: performer legal/family discovery and a photograph of a parents' building expose stalking risk; an altered explicit image is refused for display; crash-photo metadata and exact locations must not publish. Polygraphs are not reliable truth machines and EXIF proves only limited facts. Adult-industry labor discussion covers agency reputation, invasive verification, career transition, performer autonomy and the useful but bounded craft lesson that reliability matters when notice and terms are fair. Medical metadata rejects claims that frequent sex or tampons determine vaginal tightness, that sexual activity guarantees cleanliness, and that prolonged colonics/lipo/fasting are safe retreat ideas. The Unnuttable proposal then tries to recruit Morgan as a lower-cost replacement: she asks about pay, discloses another relationship, reacts to 24/7 filming, asks to think, and says stop during career-benefit pressure. There is no deal. Later, Khalyla describes reconciliation with Bobby alongside publication betrayal, lost financial/housing power, heavy Valium use, self-directed violence and suicidal ideation. She reasserts economic autonomy and says she must love herself more. The room again turns suicide into a November 2 spectacle before direct discouragement and a denial of current intent. The final live segment ends before an appended replay of the earlier phone call, followed by damaged When the Bullies Fall lyrics. Literal speech remains uncensored; corrections, scope limits and discovery safety remain separate.

source_notes.claim: Polygraphs are about 90% accurate and could soon replace lawyers/courts.
source_notes.assessment: Incorrect and overconfident. The American Psychological Association says independent scientific evidence does not support polygraphs as reliable and valid deception detectors; physiological arousal has many causes and error rates matter.

source_notes.claim: A polygraph is a lie detector.
source_notes.assessment: The U.S. Department of Justice states that there is no literal lie detector: the device records physical responses that may or may not relate to deception, and federal use/admissibility is limited.

source_notes.claim: Frequent sex makes a vagina permanently tighter, while tampons risk making it looser.
source_notes.assessment: Unsupported. Pelvic support involves muscles and connective tissue and can be affected by pregnancy, childbirth, aging and other factors; the episode's simple sex/tampon rule is not clinical guidance.

source_notes.claim: Every photo carries reliable time and location metadata that proves when and where it was made.
source_notes.assessment: Overstated. This episode's old-photo date was ultimately admitted, but metadata may be unavailable, stripped, altered or copied and should not be published as a location trail. General online-image privacy also remains limited.

speaker_policy: Public cast and Morgan Lee may be identified at episode level where introduced. Legal names, family members, family buildings, exact routes, crash metadata, private partners, sex workers/clients, message addresses and the prospective show's workers stay excluded from discovery. Overlap, nudity, physical contact, crying calls, phone replay and trivia punishment require acoustic/video validation. No line-level named dialogue publishes until held-out voice validation passes.
